subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should OpenClaw treat LiteLLM/Vertex beta generic 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` as a recoverable provider/session request-shape error, and which recovery action should own it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe behavior depends on live provider proof and maintainer intent because `INVALID_ARGUMENT` can mean context pressure, malformed transcript, media/schema rejection, or an unrecoverable provider validation failure.

options.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
options.body: Use live LiteLLM/Vertex evidence to add a narrowly scoped classifier plus user-facing recovery and lane cleanup without broadening all `INVALID_ARGUMENT` handling.

options.title: Context-overflow-only treatment
options.body: Only classify this route as context overflow when provider details prove token/context pressure and then reuse compaction or larger-model fallback semantics.

options.title: Keep as manual diagnosis
options.body: Leave generic `INVALID_ARGUMENT` unclassified until reporters provide live traces that distinguish request-shape, context, media, and auth/provider causes.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Use live LiteLLM/Vertex evidence to add a narrowly scoped classifier plus user-facing recovery and lane cleanup without broadening all `INVALID_ARGUMENT` handling.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the adjacent provider-error normalization work and commented on classifier completeness, making them the best available owner for the provider failover policy choice.
